 New Yorkers will cast their ballots on Tuesday to decide who will represent them in the House of Representatives.
 These New York Congressional Races May Decide the House
 By
 Alexangel Ventura 
 Nov 2, 2026 2:58 am 
 · Updated Nov 2, 2026 2:58 am 
 Reading time: about 7 minutes
 While New York State frequently votes Democratic at the state and federal levels, local U.S. House elections will have tighter races to watch. Below, The Sun has listed key House races to watch on Tuesday, including the race between Rep. Josh Riley (D-N.Y.) and his Republican challenger Peter Oberacker (R-N.Y.).
 New York’s 17th District: Mike Lawler vs. Cait Conley 
 In New York’s largely suburban and rural 17th district, which includes parts of Putnam, Dutchess, Westchester and Rockland counties, incumbent Rep. Mike Lawler (R-N.Y.) is being challenged by Democrat and national security official Cait Conley. 
 The district has historically favored House Democrats since 2012, when former Rep. Sean Patrick Maloney (D-N.Y.) persisted in areas now within the present-day district, winning five consecutive elections. 
 It was only in 2022 that the district flipped Republican, largely due to strong downballot effects from the governor’s race between Gov. Kathy Hochul (D-N.Y.) and then-Rep. Lee Zeldin (R-N.Y.). 
 Lawler benefited from Republican shifts in the region since Lee Zeldin’s 2022 gubernatorial campaign, including among Jewish voters , and his widely characterized moderate voting record made him appealing to suburban voters less keen on President Donald Trump.
 However, Cait Conley’s economically-focused campaign agenda , combined with President Trump’s reported low approval in the district, is making this district one of the closest races this election season. To date, more than a combined $40 million has been spent by both sides, making it one of the most expensive races in the nation. 
 Many analysts rated this district as a toss-up, including election data and real-time reporting company Decision Desk HQ , with polls showing a relatively even split between the candidates. Emerson College had Conley up by 2% in September, while McLaughlin & Associates had Lawler up by 3% in the same month.
 New York’s 3rd District: Tom Suozzi vs. Mike LiPetri 
 In northern parts of Long Island, including North Hempstead and Glen Cove, incumbent Rep. Tom Suozzi (D-N.Y.) is being challenged by former State Assemblyman Mike LiPetri (R-N.Y.).
 The wealthy suburban district, which Donald Trump won at the federal level in 2024 by a 4% margin, elected Suozzi on the same ballot. Suozzi won a special election to replace Rep. George Santos (R-N.Y.) after he was expelled from Congress following criminal charges of wire fraud and money laundering. LiPetri was the Republican nominee on that same 2024 ballot.
 Trump’s low approval ratings may benefit Suozzi in November. However, Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman’s (R-N.Y.) campaign for governor could help Republicans down-ballot in the county, creating a close race.
 Tom Suozzi is usually characterized as a moderate Democrat, calling himself a “common-sense Democrat.” His opponent has been endorsed by Donald Trump and campaigned on criticism of New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D-N.Y.).
 Analysts predict this race will either lean Democratic or likely Democratic . 
 New York’s 4th District: Laura Gillen vs. Jeanine Driscoll 
 In the bottom of Nassau County, which includes Hempstead, incumbent Rep. Laura Gillen (D-N.Y.) is seeking re-election against Jeanine Driscoll (R-N.Y.), the Hempstead Receiver of Taxes . 
 Similar to New York’s 3rd district, this district is a wealthy suburb, with the median household income at over $141k . Trump narrowly lost the district in 2024, while former Rep. Anthony D’Esposito (R-N.Y.) emerged victorious. D’Esposito lost re-election to Gillen in 2024.
 Gillen, named one of the most bipartisan members of Congress by the Bridge Grades report, has called for lowering costs and cutting taxes for Long Islanders. 
 Driscoll also emphasized cutting taxes, as well as providing relief for Nassau County families and seniors and restoring the State and Local Tax Deduction . She has also been endorsed by President Trump. 
 Blakeman’s gubernatorial candidacy may also have a significant impact on a Republican victory in the 4th district, since it is his home district. 
 Most analysts predict this race will be likely Democratic. 
 New York’s 1st District: Nick LaLota vs. Chris Gallant 
 On the shores of Suffolk County, including the Hamptons and Smithtown, incumbent Rep. Nick LaLota (R-N.Y.) is seeking re-election against Democrat air traffic controller Chris Gallant.
 In this middle-class district, President Trump won by a substantial margin, and LaLota defeated his Democratic opponents in 2022 and 2024 by double-digit margins. This part of Long Island has shifted Republican in recent years, with gains among Hispanic and suburban voters.
 The Republican incumbent has fought for tax cuts, environmental and water quality improvements and a stronger border. Gallant has campaigned for infrastructure investments, expanded Medicare and Medicaid and government accountability.
 While most analysts give this race a Likely Republican or Safe Republican rating, Decision Desk HQ predicts a much closer Leans Republican rating, reflecting the growing competitiveness in the district.
 New York’s 21st District: Anthony Constantino vs. Blake Gendebien 
 In the northernmost parts of New York, including Plattsburgh, Glens Falls and Potsdam, Republican businessman Anthony Constantino will contest an open race with Democrat dairy farmer Blake Gendebien. 
 This district has been solidly Republican for the past three presidential elections and for longtime incumbent Rep. Elise Stefanik (R-N.Y.). However, Trump’s reported weakness in the conservative district, along with Gendebien’s “ conservative, free-market Democrat ” campaign, has made this race more competitive than initially expected.
 Constantino is campaigning as a Trump ally, having received the President’s endorsement.
 Analysts have given the race a Lean Republican or Likely Republican characterization, receiving the closest rating for the area of the current district in sixteen years .
 A recent Siena University poll showed Gendebien leading Constantino by 4%.
 New York’s 19th District: Josh Riley vs. Peter Oberacker 
 Comprising Ithaca and Binghamton, incumbent Rep. Josh Riley (D-N.Y.) is seeking re-election against State Senator Peter Oberacker (R-N.Y.).
 The 19th district has remained competitive since 2018, switching from Antonio Delgado (D-N.Y.) to Marc Molinaro (R-N.Y.) to Riley, who narrowly flipped the seat from Molinaro in 2024 in the most expensive House race in the country.
 Incumbent Riley is campaigning on holding utility companies accountable for raising rates, housing construction, fighting monopolies and banning corporate PAC money. 
 During his time in the House, he has voted to block federal aid to universities that boycott “major strategic partners,” such as Israel . In his last term he sponsored 17 bills, three of which target utility companies and two bills to expand access to reproductive care. Riley also voted against four bills that would limit access to Planned Parenthood services. 
 Oberacker, meanwhile, is calling for protecting law enforcement, reducing taxes and supporting rural communities. As a state senator, his focus is on supporting emergency services and agriculture, along with expanding high speed internet access to rural places.  
 Oberacker recently lost support from MAGA Majority , an initiative that supports Republican non-incumbent campaigns, after he posted a picture of his grandfather in a Nazi uniform on Veterans Day. Oberacker captioned the post, “I salute all who served,” and later told Politico it was the only picture he had of his late grandfather. 
 Analysts have this race as Likely Democratic or Safe Democratic .
 Alexangel Ventura 
 Alexangel Ventura is a member of the class of 2030 in the Dyson School of Applied Economics & Management. He is a news contributor and can be reached at av648@cornell.edu.
